newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX ends the day at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX ends the day at higher levels.

text.p: German equities ended the day at higher levels on Tuesday, underpinned by a stronger dollar and upbeat opening on Wall Street but lacking significant new data to help the market find new direction.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended at 3,348.90 points, up 20.49 points or 0.62 percent, stuck in the middle of a narrow trading range which saw it reach a high of 3,357.75 points and a low of 3,325.75 points.
Earlier its bourse counterpart, the DAX index, ended the day at 3,340.33 points, down 7.25 points or 0.22 percent.
"It's all a bit drifty this afternoon. We had a busy morning with lots of corporate data, but this afternoon the index is virtually unchanged," said a Frankfurt broker.
The strongest gainer in afternoon IBIS trade was Deutsche Lufthansa AG, which ended up 1.22 marks, or 5.54 percent, at 23.25 marks.

Dealers said that there was positive sentiment in the market on the course of the airline's privatisation programme, while other dealers said that there were technical reasons for the share's upward mobility.
Also performing strongly in late electronic trade was chemical giant Hoechst AG, which ended up 1.93 points, or nearly three percent, at 66.90 marks.
Dealers said that Hoechst stock had underperformed its counterparts in the chemical sector for some time, and was undergoing a delayed reaction.
They said the stability of the dollar also helped.
Shares in software group SAP AG rose strongly after it reported a 54 percent jump in first quarter pre-tax profits to 181 million marks on sales rising almost as strongly to 1.03 billion marks.
Preference shares in SAP ended up 6.40 marks, a rise of 2.20 percent, at 297.50 marks.

Electronics giant Siemens also ended higher, up up 1.15 marks, or 1.28 percent, at 90.90 marks, off earlier peaks, amid high market expectations of strong first-half 1996/97 figures when the group reports on Wednesday.
The market was further underpinned by a stronger opening on the Dow Jones Industrial index, while weaker-than-expected inflation figures from North Rhine-Westphalia underpinned sentiment.
